summary: Split the long Karma Quest home rotation E2E scenario while retaining cross-layout continuity and real journey-start checks

spec.reason: The game rules and user-visible behavior are unchanged; only browser test structure and diagnostic output changed.

design.reason: Portrait, landscape, compact layout, panel closing, and journey-start expectations remain in the browser tests.

validation: PR #395 Browser E2E run 39713747115 attempt 1: 82 passed, 1 skipped, 2 failed; the home rotation scenario exhausted its whole-test 30-second budget and best-year transition timed out. Unchanged attempt 2 passed 84 with 1 skipped; no root cause was established.

PR #397 head 527f6fa Browser E2E run 39722581398: 83 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed; the same home rotation scenario exhausted its whole-test 30-second budget at the final journey-start assertion. The best-year scenario passed.

The original scenario was divided into two independently bounded tests. The first checks home information through portrait, landscape, and compact rotations and closure; the second checks character information through compact-to-landscape rotation, closure, and a single real journey-start tap. That final rotation tap reads canvas geometry and backing size in one browser snapshot after layout readiness; the existing shared touch helper remains unchanged.

Local Chromium runs: both revised scenarios passed 4 of 4 each; the strengthened journey phase and loading-state assertion passed 4 more runs. The full Karma Quest Chromium suite passed 85 with its existing 1 skip; typecheck and lint passed.

On head 8cfb4d1, WebKit CI run 39725262580 passed 51 tests and failed the progress-storage-write journey test because year 2 did not advance to year 3 within 5 seconds. Local WebKit reproduced the same transition failure in 9 of 10 runs with the faster atomic touch helper. Reverting only that helper locally passed 6 of 6, supporting a rendered-input readiness race rather than a changed storage rule.

Waiting only for one report frame and selected-row/button state still left 3 of 10 local WebKit failures with the fast shared touch helper. A wider WebKit subset then exposed unrelated fast-tap regressions, so the shared helper was restored. The focused storage test still verifies a visible, enabled report button, a real accepted submit input, and the production transition before the original stage advancement assertion. With those checks, it passed 10 of 10 local WebKit repeats without retry taps or extended timeouts.

The first home-information tap also missed before the home rail was rendered in a mixed WebKit run (3 of 3 failures). Waiting for the visible enabled rail and two rendered frames kept the single real tap and passed all five combined storage/rotation cases in three subsequent runs (15 of 15). The exact 52-test WebKit CI subset then passed locally.

PR #397 head 8cfb4d1 Browser E2E run 39725262594: 83 passed, 1 skipped, 2 failed; best-year and twelve-year journeys stayed in battle after the original 5-second report wait. The rotation case passed. The revised tests preserve the same natural timer and 5-second assertion, and write scene clock/frame/timer state to the existing CI artifact path only if the assertion fails. Both scenarios passed three local Chromium runs each; best-year also passed three runs with a local sixfold CPU throttle.
limitations: The original CI logs do not distinguish a missed final tap from delayed journey art loading. The revised journey assertion exposes phase, journeyPending, and journeyError; on failure the existing CI artifact path also saves accepted game-object input events, scene/frame state, timing, and canvas geometry. The cause remains unproven until a failing run supplies state evidence.

Playwright error-context files are not uploaded by the current workflow. The new focused failure JSON uses its existing screenshots artifact path. The known best-year timing failure remains separately tracked in docs/TODO.md.

A passing local run does not establish that the revised exact-head CI will pass. The exact point of the original CI missed input is not directly captured by its screenshot-only artifact; the local comparison and code path support the readiness-race explanation.

The two CI battle-to-report failures have no frame or scene-clock evidence yet, so scheduling starvation versus another cause remains unresolved until a failing diagnostic JSON is captured. No production timer or test timeout was changed.
